title: Accepted Review Provider Mapping Application
problem: Accepted Metadata Candidate Reviews are durable, but applying them to Provider Subject and Provider Mapping state must be a named backend service rather than a hidden status-transition side effect.
gates: JSONL validation for docs/workstreams/accepted-review-provider-mapping-application/TASKS.jsonl, CAMPAIGNS.jsonl, and CONTEXT.jsonl
cargo nextest run -p nako-db candidate_review provider_mapping --no-fail-fast

evidence.summary: Opened the accepted-review Provider Mapping application lane from MCDR closeout and selected a read-only application plan as the first executable task.
Added read-only accepted-review Provider Mapping application plans with action/reason/source semantics and tests proving no Provider Mapping writes during planning.

Added an idempotent accepted-review application service that writes only the root Provider Subject and accepted Provider Mapping, protects rejected mappings, and keeps related graph nodes preview-only.

Split Admin API/Web mutation scope to proposed:admin-web-provider-depth-governance after source coverage showed existing Provider Mapping review routes do not cover durable Candidate Review application.
Closed the backend accepted-review Provider Mapping application lane and recorded Admin/Web governance plus related-node hierarchy follow-ons.

architecture_refs.capability: Accepted review Provider Mapping application closed evidence

continue_policy.notes: This lane is closed. Open proposed:admin-web-provider-depth-governance before exposing durable Candidate Review evidence or accepted-review application through Admin API/Web.
